data.title: KSrelief Implements 1,304 Child-Focused Projects Worth over $1.339 Billion
data.content:
Riyadh, November 20, 2026, SPA -- The King Salman Humanitarian Aid and Relief Center (KSrelief) has implemented 1,304 projects for children worth more than $1.339 billion, benefiting 304,607,788 children, as it marks World Children's Day on November 20.
    Saudi Arabia's humanitarian work through KSrelief focuses on reaching children affected by crises and conflicts, many of whom have lost their homes or been deprived of medical care and education, and on understanding their needs before they can voice them.
    Among KSrelief's specialized programs is an initiative in Yemen to rehabilitate children formerly recruited by the terrorist Houthi militia, which provides psychological and social support to the children and their families and helps them return to school and reintegrate into society.
    Its Saudi hearing volunteer program provides cochlear implants and auditory rehabilitation for children in Tunisia, Syria, Türkiye, Senegal, Kenya, and Somalia, as well as Palestinian children in Jordan, and is described as the world's largest humanitarian volunteer effort in cochlear implantation and auditory rehabilitation.
    KSrelief has also strengthened its partnership with UNICEF to help millions of children worldwide through healthcare, nutrition programs for newborns and mothers, continued education in disaster and crisis areas, and educational supplies. In 2025, it signed agreements with the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF to protect 370 million children a year against polio.
    Over 36 years, the Saudi Conjoined Twins Programme has carried out 75 separation surgeries and evaluated 160 cases from 29 countries on five continents. The first operation, in 1990, was led by Advisor at the Royal Court, Supervisor General of KSrelief, and head of the program's medical and surgical team Dr. Abdullah Al Rabeeah. The Ministry of Defense provides medical transport for the twins, King Abdullah Specialist Children's Hospital of the Ministry of National Guard hosts, diagnoses, treats, and separates them, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs issues their visas through its missions abroad.
    KSrelief also received the 2024 Family and Child-Friendly Institution award from the Arab League General Secretariat's Department of Family and Childhood in recognition of its support for Palestinian children and families living under occupation.
    Through KSrelief, the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia reaffirms its commitment to children worldwide, regardless of language or birthplace, and to building a better future for them.
    -- SPA
